review_notes: I read the whole file and the lemmas it depends on in GeneralLinearCoordinateRing.lean (evaluate_matrix, evaluate_detInverse, toGL_apply). I also checked the uses of the new lemmas elsewhere in formal-frontier. I found no loop or competing-rule risk. The one issue is an incomplete simp interface: the matrix-entry lemma isn't simp, but its detInverse sibling is. I couldn't run Lean. The claim that the entry lemmas would fire as simp lemmas rests on reading their statements, not on testing. I did not check whether the new simp lemma would interact badly with other simp sets, though I saw no conflicting rule.

findings.excerpt:
theorem generalLinearGroupMulEquivAlgHom_apply_matrix
    (g : Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup n R) (i j : n) :
    (generalLinearGroupMulEquivAlgHom K n R g).ofConv (matrix K n i j) = g i j :=
findings.problem: The two coordinate-evaluation lemmas for `generalLinearGroupMulEquivAlgHom` are treated differently. The `detInverse` one is `@[simp]`, and so is `generalLinearGroupMulEquivPoints_apply_left`. The matrix-entry one is not. Yet evaluating the equivalence on an entry `matrix K n i j` is just as canonical, and the right-hand side `g i j` is strictly simpler. The underlying `evaluate_matrix` in the algebra file is also not simp. Downstream code therefore has to name the lemma in `rw`: GeneralLinearDeterminantSection.lean line 314 does this in the middle of a proof, and the test file does it with `rw [generalLinearGroupMulEquivAlgHom_apply_matrix]`. Because `generalLinearGroupMulEquivAlgHom` is a plain `def` (a `MulEquiv` into `WithConv`), simp cannot unfold it. A `simp` call on `... (matrix K n i j)` therefore gets stuck, unlike the `detInverse` case.
findings.proposed_change: Mark the lemma `@[simp]`. Its LHS head is the `ofConv` of the coerced equivalence applied to a `matrix K n i j` generator, and it is non-looping because it rewrites to `g i j`, with the same hypotheses as the `detInverse` simp lemma. Optionally also make the two point-level lemmas `generalLinearGroupPoint_preimage_entry` and `generalLinearGroupPoint_preimage_detInverse` simp. Their LHS is stated with `Spec.preimage (...).left`, and the existing simp lemma `generalLinearGroupMulEquivPoints_apply_left` followed by `Spec.preimage_map` would then reach the same normal form. The `rw` steps in the proofs at lines 154 and 162 could then become `simp`.
findings.benefit: Matrix-entry and `detInverse` evaluations would both simplify to `g i j` and `↑(det g)⁻¹` automatically. Callers such as the section and diagonal files could drop explicit `rw [generalLinearGroupMulEquivAlgHom_apply_matrix]` steps and the `by_cases` simp calls would see entries directly. The simp set would be symmetric across entries and the inverse determinant.
